title: The Second Time Zumi Closed Its Doors in Nairobi
conflicts: Founders verified: William McCarren and Sabrina Dorman founded the 2016 magazine (Disrupt Africa 2017, TechBuild Africa 2019); Mohamed Nuur, Tomas Rosales and Eric Njogu joined as co-founders of the later marketplace (TechCabal, Khusoko). Closure was March 2023, not the slate's 2022. Funding $920,000 (Citizen, Business Daily, Business Today, all citing Crunchbase) versus about $970,000 (TechCabal, also Crunchbase); story says under $1 million. 150 job losses as reported, though McCarren himself said only that he built a team of 150. Sales and customer figures are McCarren's own, attributed.
notes: Slate's 'funding fell through' is told as McCarren put it (fundraising became extremely difficult, not sustainable in time); no specific failed round is documented. The episode includes the earlier 2019 closure of the magazine as background. Little is documented about how the closure decision was reached beyond McCarren's LinkedIn post (quoted via Retail Technology Innovation Hub; LinkedIn itself not cited). He promised published reflections; none were found.
